title: Psychological first aid handout
description: A one-page psychological first aid handout for shelter staff, responders or parents in an exercise, listing the eight core actions in plain language. It is an original summary, not a copy of the field guide. Any support line it shows is a fictional exercise number.

examples: Harbor County Disaster Behavioral Health Team
Helping people who are upset: eight core actions
Psychological first aid is a calm, practical way to support people in the first hours and days after a frightening event. It is not counseling and you do not need to be a clinician.

coreActions.description: The eight core actions of psychological first aid, in this order: contact and engagement; safety and comfort; stabilization; information gathering; practical assistance; connection with social supports; information on coping; linkage with collaborative services

whatToDo.description: Plain-language description of what to do
examples: Introduce yourself, ask how you can help and respect the person's wishes.
Talk with a peer or supervisor after a hard shift.

whenToGetMoreHelp.description: When to bring in a clinician or the shelter mental health lead, without clinical detail
examples: If someone talks about harming themselves or others, or you are worried they are not safe, stay with them and tell the shelter mental health lead right away.

exerciseHelpline.description: A fictional exercise line for the scenario, never a real number

attribution.description: Source and note that this is an original summary
examples: Based on the eight core actions in the Psychological First Aid Field Operations Guide (NCTSN and National Center for PTSD, 2nd edition, 2006); this handout is an original summary for the exercise.
